newsitem.title: CHILE: Endesa eyes move into Colombia, Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Endesa eyes move into Colombia, Mexico.

text.p: Chilean power firm Empresa Nacional de Electricidad SA (Endesa), will lead consortia to bid in power sector privatizations in Colombia and Mexico, the company said.
In both countries, Endesa said it teamed up with foreign and local companies to bid in auctions beginning this year. The company is Chile's largest power generator.

In Colombia, Endesa created a consortium with U.S. company NRG Energy Inc and local firm Corporacion Financiera del Valle SA and has a "special interest" in two of the seven power stations to be privatized in December, it said.
One of the power plants, Bethania, has 500 MW production capacity and the other, Chivor, has 1,000 MW, it said.
Endesa will hold a 51 percent stake in the consortium, while NRG holds 25 percent and the local firm, known by its acronym Corfivalle, holds the remaining 24 percent.
In Mexico, Endesa said it signed onto a consortium with U.S. firm Entergy and Japan's Mitsui to bid in the Mrida III electricity project in the state of Yucatn.
The project, to be auctioned by Mexico's Federal Electricity Commission, calls for building and operating a gas- and diesel-powered plant of 440 MW, Endesa said.
